parsedVerdict.reasoning: AuthService is declared application-layer. Its use-case orchestration fits that role: login, social login, registration, email confirmation, password reset, profile update and token refresh, all done by calling UsersService, SessionService and MailService. But the file also builds HTTP transport responses throughout. It throws UnprocessableEntityException, NotFoundException and UnauthorizedException from @nestjs/common, and puts explicit HTTP status codes (HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND) inside the error bodies. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes and response shapes is a presentation/transport job. It is also inline low-level infrastructure work: password checks with bcrypt.compare, session-hash creation with crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex'), and direct JWT signing and verifying with secrets read from ConfigService (getTokensData, register, confirmEmail, forgotPassword, resetPassword, update). These belong behind infrastructure ports (password hasher, token issuer). The HTTP coupling is the clearest misplaced responsibility, so the unit fails.

Mapping errors to HTTP is a presentation/transport job.

These belong behind infrastructure adapters.
